n: David asks the Lord to hear his just cause and his honest prayer — words from sincere lips.
Let God’s verdict come from his presence; let his eyes see what is right.
God has examined David’s heart at night and tested him, finding nothing wrong. David has resolved not to sin with his mouth.

f.w: I am purposed that my mouth shall not transgress

n: Guided by God’s word, David has avoided the ways of violent people.

f.w: by the word of thy lips

n: His steps have held to God’s paths, and his feet have not slipped. (Hebrew can be read as a statement or a prayer.)
David calls on God, confident he will answer: “Turn your ear to me and hear.”
Show your wonderful steadfast love, you who save those who seek refuge at your right hand.

f.g: Hebrew ḥesed — loyal, covenant love, shown in a wondrous way.
The hand of power and favor.

n: A tender plea: guard me like the pupil of your eye, hide me in the shadow of your wings. God protects what is most precious to him.

f.g: The pupil — the most guarded, precious part of the eye.
Like a mother bird sheltering her young.

n: …from the wicked who attack him and from deadly enemies who surround him.
They have closed their hearts — callous and fat with prosperity — and speak arrogantly.

f.g: Their hearts are hardened and insensitive.

n: They track David’s steps and surround him, watching for a chance to throw him to the ground.

f.w: set their eyes bowing down to the earth
f.g: They are intent on bringing him down.

n: They are like a lion hungry for prey or a young lion crouching in ambush.

f.w: as a lion that is greedy of his prey

n: Rise up, Lord! Confront them and bring them down; rescue me from the wicked by your sword.
Save me by your hand from people whose only reward is in this life. God gives them plenty, and they pass wealth on to their children — but that is all they have.

f.w: men of the world, which have their portion in this life

n: But David’s hope is higher: he will see God’s face in righteousness and, when he awakes, be satisfied with his likeness. Many read this as a hope beyond death.

f.w: I will behold thy face in righteousness
I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness
